answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable work credential: peers issue one only after observing useful contributions across several rounds, and revoke it when later audits find copied or fabricated work. A newcomer may join, but cannot instantly multiply voting weight by minting identities; each fake must earn trust through costly, repeated tasks. Like a garden shaped by the tide, reputation changes gradually, while a stolen relic of past work cannot be replayed as fresh proof.
